title: Interlocking Driveway Lifespan Ontario: How Long Pavers Really Last
seoTitle: Interlocking Driveway Lifespan Ontario | Paver Longevity Barrie
seoDescription: A properly installed interlocking driveway in Ontario will last 25-50+ years, depending on the base preparation, paver quality, and regular maintenance.
tldr: In Ontario, a professionally installed interlocking driveway has a lifespan of 25 to 50 years, and often longer. This longevity is almost entirely dependent on the quality of the base. A driveway built on a 12-to-16-inch compacted clear stone base will outlast our harsh freeze-thaw cycles, while one on a minimal 6-inch base will likely fail within 10 years. The choice of an 80mm thick paver from a reputable brand like Permacon or Unilock is also critical for handling vehicle weight and resisting salt damage.
intro:
Every spring in Barrie, I see the same thing: heaved, sunken, and shifted driveways. Homeowners call us frustrated that their five-year-old interlock looks worse than the thirty-year-old asphalt next door. The problem isn't the pavers themselves; it's what's underneath them. The single biggest factor determining an interlocking driveway's lifespan in our Simcoe County climate isn't the brand of stone or the colour you picked—it's the depth and type of aggregate used for the base.

Companies trying to win bids on price alone will cut corners here, laying pavers on a shallow 6-inch base of granular 'A' that holds water. When that water freezes, it expands and pushes everything up. Here, with our heavy clay soil and wild temperature swings from -20°C to +5°C in a single week, that's a recipe for failure. A proper interlocking driveway is an engineered system designed to manage water and frost, not just a pretty surface.

This isn't just about looks. A failed driveway is a liability, a tripping hazard, and a constant source of frustration. Understanding what makes a paver installation last for decades versus a handful of years is the most important step you can take before investing your hard-earned money.

sections.heading: What Actually Determines an Interlocking Driveway's Lifespan?
sections.html:
The longevity of an interlocking driveway is 90% dependent on its foundation. The pavers you see are just the surface; the real work happens in the 12 to 16 inches of base material below. In Simcoe County, we deal with heavy clay soil that retains moisture. When this moisture freezes, it causes 'frost heave,' pushing the ground (and your driveway) upwards. A poorly constructed base can't handle this pressure, leading to the sinking and shifting you see on failed projects.

The industry standard, as set by the Interlocking Concrete Pavement Institute (ICPI), is a minimum base depth, but we believe the minimum isn't enough for our region. We exclusively install a base of at least 12 inches (30 cm) of compacted 3/4" clear stone for all driveways. This is significantly more robust than the 6-8 inches some contractors use. Why clear stone instead of cheaper granular 'A'? Clear stone has voids between the particles, allowing water to drain straight through and away from the surface. Granular 'A' contains fine particles that trap water right under your pavers, which is the primary cause of heaving.

This deep, free-draining base creates a stable foundation that isn't susceptible to frost. Each layer of our base is compacted in 4-inch lifts using a heavy-duty plate compactor that delivers at least 5,000 pounds of centrifugal force. This ensures over 98% standard proctor density, meaning the base is solid and won't settle over time. It's an investment in excavation and material, but it's the only way to build a driveway in Barrie that will last 30, 40, or even 50 years.

sections.heading: How Do Ontario's Freeze-Thaw Cycles Affect Pavers?
sections.html:
Ontario's winters, especially around Lake Simcoe, are defined by the freeze-thaw cycle. Temperatures can swing from -15°C overnight to +5°C the next day. This cycle is the number one enemy of any paved surface. When water penetrates the base or joints of a driveway and freezes, it expands by about 9%. This expansion exerts immense upward pressure, forming 'ice lenses' that can lift entire sections of pavers.

A correctly engineered system anticipates this. As mentioned, a 12-16 inch clear stone base is the first line of defence, giving water a path to escape before it can freeze. The second critical component is the jointing sand. We use high-quality polymeric sand, like Techniseal HP NextGel, on every project. This isn't just regular sand; it contains a polymer that activates with water and hardens to form a durable, flexible joint. This hardened sand serves two purposes: it locks the pavers together horizontally, but more importantly, it creates a semi-impermeable barrier that prevents surface water from washing down into the base material.

Without effective polymeric sand, water seeps into the bedding course (the 1-inch layer of sand directly under the pavers), saturates it, and then freezes. This is what causes individual pavers or small sections to pop up. We see it all the time on jobs we're called to repair. Proper sand, installed correctly and topped up every 5-7 years, is essential for keeping the system intact and preventing water from becoming a destructive force.

sections.heading: Does Paver Quality and Thickness Really Matter?
sections.html:
While the base is the most critical factor for longevity, the quality of the paver itself plays a significant role in how your driveway looks and performs over decades. For any surface that will see vehicle traffic, we only use pavers that are at least 80mm (about 3.15 inches) thick. Patio stones are often 60mm thick, which is perfectly fine for foot traffic but will not stand up to the weight of an SUV or a delivery truck over time. The extra 20mm of thickness provides substantially more structural strength and load distribution.

Beyond thickness, we look at two key technical specifications: compressive strength and water absorption. Reputable manufacturers like Unilock, Permacon, and Techo-Bloc produce pavers with a compressive strength exceeding 8,000 PSI (pounds per square inch). This means a single paver can withstand the weight of four mid-sized cars stacked on top of it before crushing. Lower quality, 'big-box store' pavers may only be rated to 5,000 PSI, making them more susceptible to cracking and spalling.

Water absorption rate, governed by the ASTM C936 standard, should be below 5%. Pavers that absorb more water are more vulnerable to damage during freeze-thaw cycles, as the water freezing inside the paver itself causes the surface to flake away (spalling). Top-tier manufacturers use advanced processes to create dense pavers with low absorption rates and often include proprietary colour blends that resist fading from UV exposure. Choosing a quality paver is a long-term investment in the durability and appearance of your driveway.

sections.heading: The Role of Ongoing Maintenance in Driveway Longevity
sections.html:
A 50-year driveway isn't a 'set it and forget it' installation. While a well-built interlock driveway is low-maintenance, it is not zero-maintenance. A few simple, seasonal tasks can dramatically extend its life and keep it looking great. The most important maintenance task is cleaning and sealing. We recommend sealing your interlocking driveway every 3-5 years, depending on traffic and sun exposure. A good quality, breathable sealer protects the pavers from UV fading, oil stains, and, most importantly, de-icing salt.

Speaking of salt, this is critical for Ontario homeowners: do not use regular rock salt (sodium chloride) on your pavers. It is highly corrosive and will accelerate the deterioration of the paver surface. Instead, use products that are rated for concrete pavers, such as calcium chloride or magnesium chloride. Better yet, use a plastic shovel or a snowblower with the blade set about half an inch high to clear snow, minimizing the need for de-icers altogether. For more tips, check out our guide to preventing winter damage to your interlock.

Finally, inspect your joints annually. Over years, the polymeric sand can wear down. If you see joints that are empty or filled with dirt, it's time for a touch-up. A simple top-up prevents weeds from taking root (they grow in the dirt that collects in the joints, not from underneath) and stops water from getting into the base. This simple 2-3 hour job every few years protects the multi-thousand-dollar investment underneath.

faqs.question: Will my interlocking driveway sink?
faqs.answer: A correctly installed interlocking driveway will not sink. Sinking is almost always caused by an inadequate base; a driveway built on a compacted 12-16 inch clear stone base is engineered to handle vehicle loads and Barrie's clay soil without settling.

faqs.question: How often should you seal an interlocking driveway in Ontario?
faqs.answer: In Ontario's climate, you should seal your interlocking driveway every 3 to 5 years. Sealing protects the pavers from UV fading, stains, and damage from de-icing salts, significantly extending their cosmetic and structural life.

faqs.question: Can you plow an interlocking driveway?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can plow an interlocking driveway safely. Use a plow with a rubber or polyurethane cutting edge (UHMW plastic) and ensure the blade is set about 1/4 to 1/2 inch above the paver surface to avoid catching an edge.

faqs.question: What is the cost difference between interlock and asphalt in Barrie?
faqs.answer: In the Barrie area, a professionally installed interlocking driveway typically costs between $20 and $35 per square foot. Asphalt is significantly cheaper upfront, usually $5 to $10 per square foot, but its shorter lifespan and higher maintenance needs often make interlock a better long-term investment.

faqs.question: Do interlocking pavers fade over time?
faqs.answer: High-quality pavers from brands like Techo-Bloc or Unilock use special manufacturing processes to ensure colour is consistent throughout the stone, which minimizes fading. While some minor colour softening can occur over 20+ years of UV exposure, regular sealing every 3-5 years will keep them looking vibrant.

faqs.question: Why do weeds grow between pavers?
faqs.answer: Weeds do not grow up from the base of a properly installed driveway. They germinate from seeds that blow in and land in dirt and organic debris that accumulates in the joints over time. Using polymeric sand and power washing the surface every couple of years prevents this from happening.

faqs.question: Is a thicker paver better for a driveway?
faqs.answer: Yes, a thicker paver is essential for a driveway. The industry standard is an 80mm (3.15 inch) thick paver to withstand the weight and dynamic loads of vehicles. Using a thinner 60mm paver, which is designed for patios and walkways, will likely lead to cracking and failure.
